isolation: Explicit access restrictions; not an OS filesystem jail. No implementation, repository, history, external documentation, or source outside this directory read.

test_accesses.source: Synthetic fixtures created inside temporary subdirectories of this isolated directory, then deleted; no upstream callers used.
test_accesses.executables: python3 and cc resolved via shutil.which; subprocess cwd explicitly set to this directory.
test_accesses.compiler: C11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror with generated public-API stubs only. Syntax check covers braced ROM constructors; option=0/1 executables verify optional locals and a later unconditional descriptor index. All generated stubs/executables remain in isolated temporary directories and are deleted by tests.
test_accesses.other: Standard-library Python imports; no external sites, git commands, parent repository reads, original headers, previous replacements or session logs.

limitations: Candidate C/H files must be read to establish target usage and SPDX licence eligibility; only eligible target callers are translated.
A lexical source converter does not execute the C preprocessor: live conditional branches are scanned; supported include directives include backslash continuations.
Parser macros must be standalone statements in a compound scope; unbraced control-flow bodies are rejected to preserve declaration scope.
Synthetic API stub compilation verifies C syntax/scoping and braced ROM initializers, not real MicroPython behavior or actual callers.
Filesystem checks reject symlinks and overlap but are not a sandbox and do not eliminate adversarial concurrent filesystem races.
Conditional descriptors support complete, comma-separated descriptors with unique identifiers across the whole invocation. Other explicitly rejected shapes are listed in contract-clarifications.json.
